messages.author: 96a78639336ed702
messages.subject: Identifying pairwise relationships of quasi-landmarks from 3D facial point could
parts:
Hi all,

I have a sample of 3D facial image which is cropped using Meshmonk software (https://github.com/TheWebMonks/meshmonk) through rigid registration of a template. This software has been used in a recent paper in Nature Genetics ("Genome-wide mapping of global-to-local genetic effects on human facial shape") for cropping 3D facial images.

Applying Meshmonk to one of my facial images, I get the following point cloud


Coordinate data for this cropped file is attached as the Sample.nts file.


Since this cropped face is not symmetrized, I wish to use bilat.symmetry function to perfom GPA. I need to know from the Sample.nts file which point on the left side of the face is the counterpart of which point on the right side of the face. There are 7160 quasi-landmarks and I have no idea how such correspondence information could be obtained so that I can create a suitable matrix for the land.pairs argument of the bilat.symmetry function.


Thank you.

One cannot 'symmetrize' landmark conifuragtions without identifying matched pairs across the line of symmetry. I do not know of a fool that would identify these automatically.

Dean

messages.author: 0642bc794ffb2f1b
messages.subject: Re: Identifying pairwise relationships of quasi-landmarks from 3D facial point could
parts:
Hi Iv Xiao,

If you used the facial mask that was provided with the meshmonk software, this mask has bilateral symmetrical quasi-landmarks. You can use the index needed to "relabel" the quasi-landmarks after reflection attached as a MATLAB file. Below is some code that I use in MATLAB and illustrates the two steps involved, reflect and relabel. Once reflected and relabeled, you can symmetrize the faces by taking the average between the original masked face and the reflected and relabeled masked face.

I hope this helps

function out = reflectShape(obj,ReflectIndex)
         out = clone(obj);
         out.Vertices(:,1) = -1*out.Vertices(:,1);
         out.Vertices = out.Vertices(ReflectIndex,:);
         out.FlipNormals = true;% normals are to be flipped to maintain same inside versus outside standard
end

messages.subject: Re: Identifying pairwise relationships of quasi-landmarks from 3D facial point could
parts:
Hi Claes,

Thanks a lot for taking the time to answer my is question. I could understand steps of reflection, relabeling, and average. Please let me clarify the status of symmetry for various objects:

A. The 3D facial surface mesh from 3dMD: asymmetric (no face in the world is perfectly symmetric);

B. The anthropometric mask (i.e., the template): your previous post indicated that it is symmetric, however, page 446 of the paper "Spatially-dense 3D facial asymmetry assessment in both typical and disordered growth" said "The mask (Fig. 1b), covering the facial area of interest, consisted of spatially-dense, uniformly sampled (equally distanced at 2 mm), unpaired and non-symmetrical points on an averaged facial form calculated over the healthy young adults following a bootstrapping strategy given in Claes (2007; section 5.3)", which seems to contradict symmetric template, so I am not sure whether the template is symmetric or not;

C. The facial shape represented by quasi-landmarks, obtained after mapping: should be asymmetric since human face is asymmetric, whether a symmetric or asymmetric template is used for mapping (not sure if such understanding is correct). Implication of this issue is as follows: if the shape represented by the quasi-landmarks is symmetric, I will directly use gpagen function in geomorph for Procrustes superimposition, which will yield symmetric procrustes shape coordinates; if, however, the shape represented by the quasi-landmarks is asymmetric, I will follow your recommended reflection, relabeling, and average step before submitting the averaged shape data to gpagen, which will then yield symmetric procrustes shape coordinates.

messages.author: 0642bc794ffb2f1b
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Re: Identifying pairwise relationships of quasi-landmarks from 3D facial point could
parts:
Hi Iv Xiao,

You are right that the publication you are referring to did not make use of a bilateral symmetric mask. The one provided with Meshmonk is, and there will be a paper out soon in plos one, that has been formally accepted, about the use of this updated mask in measuring asymmetry.

Any face is indeed asymmetric, and if you require to work on symmetric shape components only, the average of the original face and its reflection is to be done.

I hope this helps

All the best

Peter

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Re: Identifying pairwise relationships of quasi-landmarks from 3D facial point could
parts:
Hi Claes,

Thanks to your help, I am now able to generate facial quasi-landmarks representing both the symmetric and asymmetric component of the face. The ReflectIndex file contained critical information regarding point-to-point symmetry. As a next step, I wish to morph this 3D quasi-landmarks into 3D surfaces (like the image from your paper below) so that I could visualize shape differences. 



For this purpose, I tried the warpRefMesh functio in geomorph R package through averagemesh <- warpRefMesh(Sample1.ply, coorddata[,,1], shape.avg). However, perhaps due to the large number of quasi-landmarks (7160) or the huge information stored in the ply file, the above function failed to run successfully on my PC (64 bit Win10, i7-7700HQ CUP, 16 GB RAM, ThinkPad). So may I please ask how did you create the 3D facial surface morphs for your study, in matlab or R? Some brief demonstrative code would be highly appreciated.

Best reards,
Lv Xiao
